MAIN ST, ROOM 1400 LOS ANGELES, CA 90012 BHAVIN PATEL 213.978.3311 ASSISTANT GENERAL MANAGER EDUARDO MAGOS ita.lacity.gov ASSISTANT GENERAL MANAGER MARIA RAMOS KAREN BASS ACTING ASSISTANT GENERAL MANAGER MAYOR September 23, 2026 REF: EXE-288-26 Honorable Members of the City Council City of Los Angeles Room 395, City Hall Los Angeles, CA 90012 Attn: Arts, Parks, and City Facilities SUBJECT: COUNCIL FILE NO. 26-1228 - EMPLOYMENT STATUS OF PREVIOUS LACITYVIEW CONTRACTOR WORKERS On September 2, 2026, the Los Angeles City Council considered and adopted an amending motion under Council File No. 26-1228 directing the Information Technology Agency (ITA), with the assistance of the Office of the City Attorney, to report on the employment status of the 41 previous contractor workers and how many transitioned to Squadron. While former contractors are under no obligation to the City of Los Angeles to disclose their current whereabouts or employment status, the ITA took a good faith effort to obtain this information for the City Council. In response to the Council’s direction, this report provides background regarding the previous Channel 35 contractor pool and its transition to the current contractor pool under Squadron. Background To supplement existing ITA employees, LA CityView Channel 35 relies on a pool of as- needed, part-time contractors to fill various production roles based on operations. The contractors provide additional production capacity and specialized skills, while the Channel 35 City employees manage the station, engage elected offices, and oversee the work performed. For the last 20 years, ITA was responsible for building and maintaining its own pool of individual production contractors. Last year, ITA requested a one-year extension of the 41 separate personal services (with a contract term of March 1, 2023 through February 28, 2026). The City Attorney approved a six-month extension and forbade a further AN EQUAL EMPLOYMENT AFFIRMATIVE ACTION EMPLOYER September 23, 2026 Page 2 extension of these contracts, citing the City Charter’s competitive contracting requirements and the need to limit sole-sourced extensions. Thus, the new expiration date was set as August 31, 2026. To comply with the City Attorney’s requirements, the ITA compiled and initiated an open, public, competitive Request For Proposals (RFP) process in early 2025. On May 9, 2025, ITA issued a Media Professional Services RFP on RampLA. Nine (9) firms submitted proposals, which were evaluated through the City's standard competitive procurement process, including pre-published scoring criteria, two rounds of proposal review, portfolio evaluation, reference checks, and compliance with the City’s contracting requirements.
